cohort: 228 neonates (102 with culture-proven sepsis and 126 with clinical sepsis)
finding: While neonates with culture-proven and clinical sepsis had comparable BP z-scores overall, low BP in the initial 54 hours of sepsis was significantly associated with in-hospital mortality, with systolic BP being the most discriminatory factor for identifying non-survivors.
mod_finding: This study found that blood pressure in the initial 54 hours following sepsis was significantly associated with in-hospital mortality in neonates, regardless of whether they were born via cesarean delivery or not.
